# [CS010] Sensitive Field Exposed in JSON Response (api-excessive-data-exposure)

A JSON response type contains a stored secret, such as a password hash, without json:"-".

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | HIGH |
| **Category** | Security |
| **CWE** | [CWE-200](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/200.html) |
| **OWASP** | A01:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

Encoding a storage model straight into a response sends every exported field, including password hashes, salts, private keys or TOTP secrets added later. The rule follows the encoded type through pointers, slices, maps and nested structs. Tag the field json:"-" or respond with a dedicated response type. Note that json:"-," still encodes the field, under the key "-".

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
type User struct {
	ID           int64  `json:"id"`
	Email        string `json:"email"`
	PasswordHash string `json:"password_hash"`
}

func list(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(users)
}
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
type User struct {
	ID           int64  `json:"id"`
	Email        string `json:"email"`
	PasswordHash string `json:"-"`
}

func list(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(users)
}
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [api-excessive-data-exposure]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    api-excessive-data-exposure: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore api-excessive-data-exposure -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** api-excessive-data-exposure
```
